#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The claude-cli backend against a fake Messages endpoint: what the model
would receive, and the step rules through real MCP calls. Runs the installed
Claude Code CLI with a dummy API key aimed at a local server, so it needs no
login, sends nothing anywhere and costs nothing. Skipped when `claude` is not
on PATH. Run it after a CLI update: the resumed session is the CLI's own
internal format.

Usage: python3 tests/project_prompt/test_claude_cli.py
"""

import http.server
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import threading
import unittest

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("run_prompt_tests", HERE / "run_prompt_tests.py")
runner = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(runner)
cli = runner.claude_cli


class FakeMessages:
    """Answers each streamed request with the next scripted response (a list
    of content blocks) and keeps every request body."""

    def __init__(self, *responses):
        self.responses, self.bodies = list(responses), []
        fake = self

        class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *_):
                pass

            def do_HEAD(self):
                self.send_response(200)
                self.end_headers()

            def do_POST(self):
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", 0))))
                if not self.path.startswith("/v1/messages") or "count_tokens" in self.path or not body.get("stream"):
                    self.send_response(404)
                    self.end_headers()
                    return
                fake.bodies.append(body)
                blocks = fake.responses.pop(0) if fake.responses else [{"type": "text", "text": "(nothing scripted)"}]
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("content-type", "text/event-stream")
                self.end_headers()

                def event(data):
                    self.wfile.write(f"event: {data['type']}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n".encode())

                event({"type": "message_start", "message": {"id": f"msg_{len(fake.bodies)}", "type": "message",
                       "role": "assistant", "model": body["model"], "content": [], "stop_reason": None,
                       "usage": {"input_tokens": 10, "output_tokens": 1}}})
                for index, block in enumerate(blocks):
                    if block["type"] == "text":
                        event({"type": "content_block_start", "index": index, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}})
                        event({"type": "content_block_delta", "index": index,
                               "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": block["text"]}})
                    else:
                        event({"type": "content_block_start", "index": index, "content_block":
                               {"type": "tool_use", "id": f"toolu_{len(fake.bodies)}_{index}", "name": block["name"],
                                "input": {}}})
                        event({"type": "content_block_delta", "index": index,
                               "delta": {"type": "input_json_delta", "partial_json": json.dumps(block["input"])}})
                    event({"type": "content_block_stop", "index": index})
                stop = "tool_use" if any(block["type"] == "tool_use" for block in blocks) else "end_turn"
                event({"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": stop, "stop_sequence": None},
                       "usage": {"output_tokens": 5}})
                event({"type": "message_stop"})

        self.server = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()


def tool(name, arguments):
    return {"type": "tool_use", "name": cli.PREFIX + name, "input": arguments}


def plain(value):
    """A request's content without the CLI's cache markers."""
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [plain(item) for item in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: plain(item) for key, item in value.items() if key != "cache_control"}
    return value


def texts(body):
    for message in body["messages"]:
        content = message["content"]
        for block in [{"text": content}] if isinstance(content, str) else content:
            yield block.get("text") or json.dumps(block.get("content", ""))


class Split(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_recorded_point_splits(self):
        """Every point becomes a session and a last message, or a session
        ending on one deferred call; mid-turn points are the deferred ones."""
        for name, request in runner.REQUESTS.items():
            items = request["body"]["input"]
            history, last, deferred = cli.split(items)
            last_item = [item for item in items if item.get("role") != "developer"][-1]
            self.assertEqual(deferred is not None, last_item.get("type") == "function_call_output", name)
            self.assertEqual(last is None, deferred is not None, name)
            cli.messages(history + (last or []))  # every item has a Messages form


@unittest.skipIf(shutil.which("claude") is None, "the Claude Code CLI is not installed")
class ThroughTheCli(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_case(self, name, *responses):
        fake = FakeMessages(*responses)
        os.environ[cli.TEST_ENDPOINT_ENV] = fake.url
        try:
            verdict, detail, _log = runner.run_once_claude(name, "INSTRUCTIONS", "claude-opus-5-5", "medium")
        finally:
            del os.environ[cli.TEST_ENDPOINT_ENV]
            fake.close()
        return verdict, detail, fake.bodies

    def assertIsolated(self, body, tools):
        self.assertEqual(body["system"][-1]["text"], "INSTRUCTIONS")
        self.assertEqual([plain(t) for t in body["tools"]],
                         [{"name": cli.PREFIX + t["name"], "description": t["description"], "input_schema": t["parameters"]}
                          for t in tools])
        for text in texts(body):  # nothing of the developer's own Claude Code setup
            self.assertNotIn("CLAUDE.md", text)
            self.assertNotIn("Output Style", text)

    def test_a_point_mid_turn(self):
        """after-preview: the turn's calls and results are replayed as real
        turns, the last call's result comes through the stub, a read the model
        makes is answered from the recording, and its change ends the run."""
        request = runner.REQUESTS["after-preview"]
        preview = runner.last_result(request)["result"]
        verdict, detail, bodies = self.run_case(
            "after-preview", [tool("workspace_inspect", {})],
            [tool("settings_apply_patch", {"expectedSessionId": preview["sessionId"],
                                           "expectedRevision": preview["revision"], "changes": {}, "scope": "process"})])
        self.assertEqual(verdict, runner.PASS, detail)
        self.assertEqual(len(bodies), 2)
        self.assertIsolated(bodies[0], runner.TOOLS)
        history, _, deferred = cli.split(request["body"]["input"])
        expected = cli.messages(history)
        sent = plain(bodies[0]["messages"])
        self.assertEqual(sent[:len(expected)], expected)
        result = sent[len(expected)]["content"][0]
        self.assertEqual(result["tool_use_id"], deferred[0]["call_id"])
        self.assertEqual([block["text"] for block in result["content"]], deferred[1])
        answered = plain(bodies[1]["messages"])[-2]["content"][-1]
        recorded = next(answer["output"] for answer in request["answers"] if answer["tool"] == "workspace_inspect")
        self.assertEqual([block["text"] for block in answered["content"]], [recorded])

    def test_a_point_on_a_new_message(self):
        """model-opened-unnamed: the person's message goes in whole, the
        plate's picture as an image and the skill as a developer message, and
        the subscription judge reads the reply."""
        runner.CLAUDE_JUDGE = ("claude-opus-5-5", "medium")
        try:
            verdict, detail, bodies = self.run_case(
                "model-opened-unnamed", [{"type": "text", "text": "That looks like a rabbit. What is it for?"}],
                [{"type": "tool_use", "name": cli.STRUCTURED_OUTPUT, "input": {"answer": "yes", "why": "a rabbit"}}])
        finally:
            runner.CLAUDE_JUDGE = None
        self.assertEqual(verdict, runner.PASS, detail)
        self.assertIsolated(bodies[0], runner.TOOLS)
        _, last, _ = cli.split(runner.REQUESTS["model-opened-unnamed"]["body"]["input"])
        sent = plain(bodies[0]["messages"])
        self.assertEqual(len(sent), 2)  # the message, and the CLI's environment note
        self.assertEqual(sent[0], cli.messages(last)[0])
        self.assertEqual([block["type"] for block in sent[0]["content"]], ["text", "text", "image", "text"])
        self.assertTrue(sent[0]["content"][-1]["text"].startswith("<developer_message>\n"))
        self.assertEqual(bodies[1]["system"][-1]["text"].split(",")[0], "You read a chat between a 3D printing app's assistant and a person")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

            def do_POST(self):
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", 0))))
                if not self.path.startswith("/v1/messages") or "count_tokens" in self.path or not body.get("stream"):
                    self.send_response(404)
                    self.end_headers()
                    return
                fake.bodies.append(body)
                blocks = fake.responses.pop(0) if fake.responses else [{"type": "text", "text": "(nothing scripted)"}]
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("content-type", "text/event-stream")
                self.end_headers()

                def event(data):
                    self.wfile.write(f"event: {data['type']}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n".encode())

                event({"type": "message_start", "message": {"id": f"msg_{len(fake.bodies)}", "type": "message",
                       "role": "assistant", "model": body["model"], "content": [], "stop_reason": None,
                       "usage": {"input_tokens": 10, "output_tokens": 1}}})
                for index, block in enumerate(blocks):
                    if block["type"] == "text":
                        event({"type": "content_block_start", "index": index, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}})
                        event({"type": "content_block_delta", "index": index,
                               "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": block["text"]}})
                    else:
                        event({"type": "content_block_start", "index": index, "content_block":
                               {"type": "tool_use", "id": f"toolu_{len(fake.bodies)}_{index}", "name": block["name"],
                                "input": {}}})
                        event({"type": "content_block_delta", "index": index,
                               "delta": {"type": "input_json_delta", "partial_json": json.dumps(block["input"])}})
                    event({"type": "content_block_stop", "index": index})
                stop = "tool_use" if any(block["type"] == "tool_use" for block in blocks) else "end_turn"
                event({"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": stop, "stop_sequence": None},
                       "usage": {"output_tokens": 5}})
                event({"type": "message_stop"})

        self.server = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()


def tool(name, arguments):
    return {"type": "tool_use", "name": cli.PREFIX + name, "input": arguments}


def plain(value):
    """A request's content without the CLI's cache markers."""
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [plain(item) for item in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: plain(item) for key, item in value.items() if key != "cache_control"}
    return value


def texts(body):
    for message in body["messages"]:
        content = message["content"]
        for block in [{"text": content}] if isinstance(content, str) else content:
            yield block.get("text") or json.dumps(block.get("content", ""))


class Split(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_recorded_point_splits(self):
        """Every point becomes a session and a last message, or a session
        ending on one deferred call; mid-turn points are the deferred ones."""
        for name, request in runner.REQUESTS.items():
            items = request["body"]["input"]
            history, last, deferred = cli.split(items)
            last_item = [item for item in items if item.get("role") != "developer"][-1]
            self.assertEqual(deferred is not None, last_item.get("type") == "function_call_output", name)
            self.assertEqual(last is None, deferred is not None, name)
            cli.messages(history + (last or []))  # every item has a Messages form


@unittest.skipIf(shutil.which("claude") is None, "the Claude Code CLI is not installed")
class ThroughTheCli(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_case(self, name, *responses):
        fake = FakeMessages(*responses)
        os.environ[cli.TEST_ENDPOINT_ENV] = fake.url
        try:
            verdict, detail, _log = runner.run_once_claude(name, "INSTRUCTIONS", "claude-opus-5-5", "medium")
        finally:
            del os.environ[cli.TEST_ENDPOINT_ENV]
            fake.close()
        return verdict, detail, fake.bodies

    def assertIsolated(self, body, tools):
        self.assertEqual(body["system"][-1]["text"], "INSTRUCTIONS")
        self.assertEqual([plain(t) for t in body["tools"]],
                         [{"name": cli.PREFIX + t["name"], "description": t["description"], "input_schema": t["parameters"]}
                          for t in tools])
        for text in texts(body):  # nothing of the developer's own Claude Code setup
            self.assertNotIn("CLAUDE.md", text)
            self.assertNotIn("Output Style", text)

    def test_a_point_mid_turn(self):
        """after-preview: the turn's calls and results are replayed as real
        turns, the last call's result comes through the stub, a read the model
        makes is answered from the recording, and its change ends the run."""
        request = runner.REQUESTS["after-preview"]
        preview = runner.last_result(request)["result"]
        verdict, detail, bodies = self.run_case(
            "after-preview", [tool("workspace_inspect", {})],
            [tool("settings_apply_patch", {"expectedSessionId": preview["sessionId"],
                                           "expectedRevision": preview["revision"], "changes": {}, "scope": "process"})])
        self.assertEqual(verdict, runner.PASS, detail)
        self.assertEqual(len(bodies), 2)
        self.assertIsolated(bodies[0], runner.TOOLS)
        history, _, deferred = cli.split(request["body"]["input"])
        expected = cli.messages(history)
        sent = plain(bodies[0]["messages"])
        self.assertEqual(sent[:len(expected)], expected)
        result = sent[len(expected)]["content"][0]
        self.assertEqual(result["tool_use_id"], deferred[0]["call_id"])
        self.assertEqual([block["text"] for block in result["content"]], deferred[1])
        answered = plain(bodies[1]["messages"])[-2]["content"][-1]
        recorded = next(answer["output"] for answer in request["answers"] if answer["tool"] == "workspace_inspect")
        self.assertEqual([block["text"] for block in answered["content"]], [recorded])

    def test_a_point_on_a_new_message(self):
        """model-opened-unnamed: the person's message goes in whole, the
        plate's picture as an image and the skill as a developer message, and
        the subscription judge reads the reply."""
        runner.CLAUDE_JUDGE = ("claude-opus-5-5", "medium")
        try:
            verdict, detail, bodies = self.run_case(
                "model-opened-unnamed", [{"type": "text", "text": "That looks like a rabbit. What is it for?"}],
                [{"type": "tool_use", "name": cli.STRUCTURED_OUTPUT, "input": {"answer": "yes", "why": "a rabbit"}}])
        finally:
            runner.CLAUDE_JUDGE = None
        self.assertEqual(verdict, runner.PASS, detail)
        self.assertIsolated(bodies[0], runner.TOOLS)
        _, last, _ = cli.split(runner.REQUESTS["model-opened-unnamed"]["body"]["input"])
        sent = plain(bodies[0]["messages"])
        self.assertEqual(len(sent), 2)  # the message, and the CLI's environment note
        self.assertEqual(sent[0], cli.messages(last)[0])
        self.assertEqual([block["type"] for block in sent[0]["content"]], ["text", "text", "image", "text"])
        self.assertTrue(sent[0]["content"][-1]["text"].startswith("<developer_message>\n"))
        self.assertEqual(bodies[1]["system"][-1]["text"].split(",")[0], "You read a chat between a 3D printing app's assistant and a person")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

All runs of all the cases run share one pool of `--jobs` workers (5 by
default, 3 for the claude-cli backend below), and each run's line gives its
wall-clock time.

## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)

`--backend claude-cli` answers every step with the locally installed Claude
Code CLI in headless mode (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude
subscription instead of a per-token API key. `--judge claude-cli` moves the
judge there as well. Neither needs a key; both need the CLI logged in once
with `claude auth login`. The runner refuses to start a run the CLI would bill
to an API key (`apiKeySource` other than the login).

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --case advice-infill --runs 1
```

The model defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` at effort `medium`, both pinned so a
count moves only when the prompt does (`--claude-model`, `--claude-effort`,
`--claude-judge-model`). `--claude-keep DIR` keeps each run's session file,
tool list, MCP config and the CLI's event stream for reading afterwards.

### Which backend for what

- **Iterating on a prompt or skill: the subscription.** A strong model
  answering the app's real requests, with real tool calls, shows what the
  prompt itself causes: an ambiguous sentence, a rule two sections disagree
  on, a skill that invites the wrong call. It costs no API money, so it can
  be run as often as the subscription's usage limits allow. Those limits are
  shared with the developer's own Claude Code work; start with one case and
  keep `--jobs` small.
- **Before a release: a small paid run on the app's default model.** The app
  defaults to `gpt-5.4-mini` (`OpenAIResponsesAgent.hpp`), which scored about
  like DeepSeek V4 Flash in the printer suite's model table. A strong model
  can paper over an ambiguity a weaker one trips on, so a pass on Opus does
  not show the shipped default will pass. That run needs Kenneth's approval
  like every paid batch.
- **The baselines below** are DeepSeek V4 Flash with the OpenAI judge. A
  claude-cli count is never compared with them. Changing the judge changes
  what every judged case counts, so `--judge claude-cli` results start their
  own baseline, under the same "confirmed results become the baseline" rule.

### How a recorded request reaches the CLI

`claude_cli.py` turns each recorded request into a CLI run, and
`claude_mcp_stub.py` serves the tools:

- **System prompt**: the rendered prompt, as `--system-prompt`.
- **Tools**: the stub is a stdio MCP server with the case's tools (the 28 of
  `project_tools.json`, or the point's own list), with their real
  descriptions and schemas. Every call the model makes reaches the runner
  through it, and the step rules above apply unchanged: a read is answered
  with the recorded answer, a change ends the run (the runner stops the CLI;
  nothing is answered), a response of reads decides or is answered whole.
- **History**: the request's items before its last turn are written as a
  session file the CLI resumes (`--resume <file>`), so earlier messages,
  calls and results reach the model as its own turns, tool calls and tool
  results, not as a transcript. The last turn's message (the person's words,
  the `<workspace>` block, the plate's picture) goes in as one stream-json
  user message.
- **A point recorded mid-turn**, after a tool result (`after-preview`,
  `after-apply`, `after-slice`, `after-intent`, `direct-change-applied`,
  `direct-change-failed`, `first-person`, `slice-refused-by-tool`): the
  session ends on that turn's last call, marked as a deferred call. The CLI
  runs it through the stub, which returns the recorded result, and then asks
  the model.

Nothing from the developer's own Claude Code setup reaches the model: no
CLAUDE.md, auto-memory, settings, hooks, output style, skills, other MCP
servers or built-in tools, a minimal environment, and an empty temporary
working directory. `test_claude_cli.py` checks that, and the shapes above,
by running the installed CLI against a fake Messages endpoint on localhost
(no login, nothing sent; about 10 seconds). Run it after a CLI update: the
session file is the CLI's internal format, verified against 2.1.283.

What differs from the app's request, beyond the model:

- **Developer messages.** The Messages API has no developer role, so each of
  the app's developer items (its notes after a file-load report, the skills)
  is a user text block wrapped in `<developer_message>` tags. Hosts that
  drop or demote the developer role raise the same question for the API
  backend.
- **The CLI's own text.** Before the prompt, the CLI sends a billing header
  and "You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK."; after
  the first message it adds a short environment note (the temporary working
  directory, platform, date and model name) and an empty system turn
  carrying the effort setting.
- **Tool names** carry the CLI's MCP prefix: the model sees
  `mcp__jusprin__settings_get`, while descriptions, which name other tools
  bare, are unchanged. The runner strips the prefix.
- **Mid-turn points**: after the deferred call's result, the CLI adds
  "Continue from where you left off." as a user message. The app's notes
  that follow the result there (the setup skill in `after-intent`, the
  slice-failed skill in `slice-refused-by-tool`) are further text blocks of
  that same tool result, since the CLI resumes no message after it.
- **Notes sent once** (a point's `once`) stay in the history after the
  first answered read; the app leaves them out of the turn's later requests.
- **Pictures** reach the model, unlike on the pinned DeepSeek hosts, so
  `model-opened-unnamed`, `model-imported-by-tool` and `model-opened-by-tool`
  can be measured here.

The usage the runner logs is the CLI's token count; on the subscription it is
not billed per token.

# Claude Code CLI as a prompt-test backend: findings (2026-10-19)

Branch `claude/claude-cli-backend`, commit ddc771948a (on jusprin-newui 170d1ae080, unmerged).

Verified against CLI 2.1.283 with a fake Messages endpoint (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + dummy key), which shows the exact request the CLI sends:

- `--bare` cannot use the subscription: it reads only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / apiKeyHelper. Not used.
- `--safe-mode` also disables `--mcp-config` servers. Not used.
- Without care the CLI injects the user's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (which holds a Sentry token), the output style and memory. Kept out with `--setting-sources ""`, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1, `--disable-slash-commands`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--tools ""`, minimal env.
- Unavoidable: billing header + "You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK." before --system-prompt; an "# Environment" system turn; an empty system turn carrying effort; MCP tool names prefixed `mcp__<server>__` (CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_MCP_NO_PREFIX has no effect on CLI-configured servers).
- MCP tools need `--allowedTools mcp__<server>` or every call is refused for permission.
- stream-json input accepts assistant messages but reorders them and drops tool results: unusable for history.
- `--resume /path/to/session.jsonl` replays a hand-written session faithfully. If it ends on a tool result, the CLI inserts an assistant "No response requested." before the new message. A session ending on a call marked with a `hook_deferred_tool` attachment resumes with no prompt: the CLI runs that call (only the last deferred one) and adds "Continue from where you left off."
- `--json-schema` works via a forced StructuredOutput tool; the answer is `structured_output` in the result event.
- Running `claude` from inside a Claude desktop session inherits that session's auth env and fails ("OAuth session expired"); the runner passes a minimal environment instead. On this Mac the standalone CLI login itself was expired (`claude auth status`: loggedIn false), so no subscription run has happened yet.
- Homebrew node is broken on this Mac (missing icu4c@78); use ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin/node for render_prompt.mjs.

"refused": I checked the plate before slicing and started nothing, so there is no slice, no estimate and nothing to print, and slicing again unchanged is refused the same way. "failed": the run started and stopped with an error partway; there is no usable slice either, and the message comes from the step that failed.

The check stops at the first problem it finds, so a slice after a fix may be refused for a different reason.

A problem counts as fixed only when a new slice no longer reports it. A change is a step towards that, not proof of it.

entries.name: mcp__ccd_session__start_session
entries.description:
Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so); the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one.

repository.description: With target "cloud", only when the user named a repository other than this project's: "owner/name" on github.com, which the cloud session clones at its default branch. Take the exact owner/name from the user's words or a listing that shows it; if you are not sure of it, ask them. A bypass or auto permission mode may not carry over: the session then starts in the cloud's default mode. If the call is refused, do not run or propose the other repository's work in this project.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

input.title: Record the reads Opus makes that the recording lacks
input.prompt:
In JusPrin's project prompt suite (tests/project_prompt), extend the recorder's "answers" lists so that two read patterns Opus 5.5 makes on the Claude subscription backend have recorded answers, then re-record requests.json.

1. settings_search with scope "object", a target {"objectId": ...} for every object on every plate, query "" and changedOnly: true. Today the runner returns no answer for any changedOnly search (recorded_answer in run_prompt_tests.py refuses it), and Opus sends exactly this first in file-note-not-instructions, print-this-no-purpose and the three model-opened/imported cases. The runner's recorded_answer has to match changedOnly searches too (scope, target, query, changedOnly; whatever limit).
2. slice_report for every plate, not only the active one (slice-refused-then-ready: Opus asks for Plate 1, id 2162, which sliced; only Plate 2's report is recorded).

Recording: the shell harness's --project-prompt-requests mode (README "What keeps it faithful to the app"); it needs the built shell harness (build/arm64/tests/shell/...). The script.json "answers" list and the harness code in tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp decide what is recorded. Keep test_steps.py and test_claude_cli.py passing, and test_openai_responses_agent.cpp's schema checks of recorded answers. Update the README's recorded-answers list. Do not run any paid API batch; checking with `--backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli` on the five affected cases (3 runs each) is fine and needs no approval beyond Kenneth's go-ahead for subscription runs. Done = those five cases have no unobserved run caused by these two reads.
input.background: The suite replays app requests recorded by the shell harness and answers only reads, only from recordings. A new --backend claude-cli (branch claude/claude-cli-backend, commit ddc771948a, on jusprin-newui) runs it on Opus 5.5 through the Claude Code CLI. Its first full batch (2026-10-19) had 10 of 63 comparable runs unobserved, nearly all because Opus asked for these two reads, which DeepSeek V4 Flash never did. Base the work on claude/claude-cli-backend so the backend is available.
